Colophon

How it’s made

The site is built with Astro into plain, static HTML. A few small parts that need to respond to you (the counting figures, the homelab readings, the triage agent, and the book filter) are React components that load on their own. Everything else is just HTML and CSS.

The type is EB Garamond, a revival of Claude Garamont’s sixteenth-century types, served from this site rather than a font CDN. The navigation is set in your system’s own sans-serif. Styles are written with Tailwind CSS.

The look borrows openly from fromjason.xyz, which reads like a person rather than a portfolio.

Where it lives

It’s self-hosted on a bare-metal Linux box at home, behind Cloudflare. There is no database and no server-side code. You can see the box’s readings, and the path a request takes to reach it, on the homelab page.

The site itself sets no cookies and runs no analytics.

Feeds & machine-readable files

  • RSS — every post, in full, for your feed reader.
  • llms.txt — a short guide to the site for language models.
  • llms-full.txt — the whole site in one Markdown file: work, case studies, books, and every post.
  • Sitemap — every public page, for search engines.
  • robots.txt — search engines and AI crawlers are welcome.
  • Raw Markdown — add .md to any post’s address for its source , like /threads/notes-from-a-homelab.md .
